context.goal: Avoid stopping the simulation on Convergence failed for educational UX

symptoms: Users hit 'Convergence failed! Element: TRA2/TRA3' frequently on stiff/idealized circuits
Reset/Start UX is disrupted by hard stop errors
root_cause: Newton iterations can fail to converge on stiff, high-Q, near-ideal circuits (e.g., transformer + transistor), especially near spikes
When timeStep can no longer be reduced below minTimeStep, the legacy behavior hard-stops

changes.summary: Add panic-mode recovery: temporary node shunts + extra junction gmin, smaller sub-iteration budget, and force-step fallback instead of stop('Convergence failed')
Relax limiter threshold in panic mode, honor simulator-provided extra gmin, and avoid hard-stopping on NaN/Inf or huge currents (clamp + converged=false)

verification.devmode: Stress-tested by configuring low transformer resistances + tiny timestep; simulation continued without stopMessage/errorMessage

tradeoffs: Accuracy is intentionally sacrificed during spikes and in panic mode
Force-step skips element updates for that step to keep UI responsive
